claim: LAMA2-related muscular dystrophy (LAMA2-MD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the LAMA2 gene.
source: LAMA2-related muscular dystrophy (LAMA2-MD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the LAMA2 gene (Zambon et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zambon et al., 2020

claim: LAMA2-MD has an estimated prevalence of 4 in 500,000 children.
source: LAMA2-MD has an estimated prevalence of 4 in 500,000 children (Nguyen et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citation to Nguyen et al., 2019

claim: LAMA2-MD accounts for 36–48% of patients with congenital muscular dystrophies (CMDs).
source: accounts for 36–48% of patients with congenital muscular dystrophies (CMDs) (Sframeli et al., 2017; Abdel Aleem et al., 2020; Ge et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citations to Sframeli et al., 2017; Abdel Aleem et al., 2020; Ge et al., 2019

claim: The LAMA2 gene is located on chromosome 6q22.33.
source: The LAMA2 gene (OMIM 156225), located on chromosome 6q22.33
evidence: Supported by established genetic knowledge and OMIM reference

claim: Laminin α2 was predominantly localized to the basal lamina of myofibers in skeletal muscle, Schwann cells in peripheral nerve, and cerebral blood vessels.
source: encodes the laminin α2 chain which was predominantly localized to the basal lamina of myofibers in skeletal muscle, Schwann cells in peripheral nerve, and cerebral blood vessels detected by immunofluorescence and immunoelectron microscopy (Leivo and Engvall, 1988; Villanova et al., 1997; Malandrini et al., 1997)
evidence: Supported by citations to Leivo and Engvall, 1988; Villanova et al., 1997; Malandrini et al., 1997

claim: Laminin α2 connects with laminin β1 and γ1 chains to form a heterotrimeric protein laminin-α2β1γ1 (LM-211).
source: Laminin α2 connects with laminin β1 and γ1 chains to form a heterotrimeric protein laminin-α2β1γ1 (LM-211).
evidence: Supported by established knowledge of laminin structure

claim: LM-211 anchors to two major groups of receptors on the cell surface: α-dystroglycan and integrins (α1β1, α2β1, α6β1, α7β1).
source: LM-211 anchors to two major groups of receptors on the cell surface, α-dystroglycan and integrins (α1β1, α2β1, α6β1, α7β1), to form dystroglycan-matrix scaffolds and regulate signal transductions (Hohenester, 2019; Durbeej, 2010; Aumailley, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hohenester, 2019; Durbeej, 2010; Aumailley, 2021

claim: The deficiency of laminin α2 in astrocytes and pericytes was associated with a defective blood-brain barrier (BBB) in the dy3K/dy3K mice.
source: It was reported that the deficiency of laminin α2 in astrocytes and pericytes was associated with a defective blood-brain barrier (BBB) in the dy3K/dy3K mice (Menezes et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Menezes et al., 2014

claim: Exons 3–4 region of the LAMA2 gene is the most frequent mutation region in patients with LAMA2-MD.
source: Our previous studies have suggested that exons 3–4 region of the LAMA2 gene is the most frequent mutation region in patients with LAMA2-MD (Tan et al., 2021; Ge et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies by the authors (Tan et al., 2021; Ge et al., 2018)

claim: A novel Lama2 knockout mouse model (dyH/dyH) was created by targeted deletion of Lama2 gene exon 3 using CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing technology.
source: Building on this finding, we utilized CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing technology to specifically delete the exon 3 of Lama2 gene, creating a novel Lama2 knockout (KO) mouse model for LAMA2-MD, named 'dyH/dyH'.
evidence: Supported by description of methods used to create the mouse model

claim: The dyH/dyH mice presented a phenotype with severe muscular dystrophy.
source: Through the analysis of phenotype, the muscle pathology, and the expression of laminin α2 protein, we confirmed that dyH/dyH mice presented a phenotype with severe muscular dystrophy.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from phenotype analysis, muscle pathology, and protein expression

claim: The dyH/dyH mice were smaller with lower weight when compared with the WT and Het mice.
source: The dyH/dyH mice were smaller with lower weight when compared with the WT and Het mice (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: The weight gain of dyH/dyH mice was delayed at postnatal days 7 (P7) and worsened through P10 to P24.
source: The weight gain of dyH/dyH mice was delayed at postnatal days 7 (P7) and worsened through P10 to P24 (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The median survival of dyH/dyH mice was 21 days (ranged from 12 to 35 days).
source: Kaplan–Meier survival analysis revealed that the median survival of dyH/dyH mice was 21 days (ranged from 12 to 35 days) (Figure 2A)
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis data shown in Figure 2A

claim: WT and Het mice were in good health throughout the observation period of one year.
source: while WT and Het mice were in good health throughout the observation period of one year.

source: At P7, the dyH/dyH mice experienced difficulties in maintaining an upright stance and righting from supine.
evidence: Supported by observational data from the study

claim: Pelvic and hindlimb muscle MRI showed significantly increased hyperintense regions on T2-weighted muscle MRI in dyH/dyH mice than in WT mice at P14 and P21.

evidence: Supported by MRI data shown in Figure 2B

claim: H&E staining showed a noticeable inequality in muscle fiber size in P7 dyH/dyH mice.

evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5C

claim: There was a decrease in astrocytes (dyH/dyH: 17.1% vs WT: 20.7%) in the dyH/dyH brain compared to WT brain.

claim: There was a decrease in glutamatergic neurons (dyH/dyH: 10.0% vs WT: 10.5%) in the dyH/dyH brain compared to WT brain.

claim: The dysfunction of cytoskeleton network-related proteins, secondary to laminin α2 deficiency, was speculated to probably impair the muscle structure and contractile function in dyH/dyH mice.
source: The dysfunction of cytoskeleton network-related proteins, secondary to laminin α2 deficiency, was speculated to probably impair the muscle structure and contractile function in dyH/dyH mice, and be associated with the degeneration and necrosis of muscle fibers (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Speculative inference based on observed cytoskeleton protein changes

claim: Muscle development-related genes, such as MyoD, Myh3, and Myof5 were upregulated in LAMA2-CMD mouse models.
source: In previous reports, muscle development-related genes, such as MyoD, Myh3, and Myof5 were upregulated in LAMA2-CMD mouse models (Mehuron et al., 2014; Onofre-Oliveira et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mehuron et al., 2014; Onofre-Oliveira et al., 2012

claim: The regeneration of muscle fibers and impaired regeneration occurred simultaneously in dyH/dyH muscles.

source: In previous reports, the expression of extracellular matrix proteins such as Col1a1, Col6α2, collagen III, fibronectin, periostin, galectin-1, and biglycan were extensively increased in LAMA2-CMD mouse models (Mehuron et al., 2014; Gawlik et al., 2019; de Oliveira et al., 2014).

claim: In the dyH/dyH mice, following laminin α2 deficiency, extracellular matrix proteins such as collagen VI and laminin α1, and several extracellular matrix protein-related genes such as Col1a2, Col5a2, Col3a1, Tnc, Fn1, and Ctss were upregulated.
source: As expected, in the dyH/dyH mice, following laminin α2 deficiency, extracellular matrix proteins such as collagen VI and laminin α1, and several extracellular matrix protein-related genes such as Col1a2, Col5a2, Col3a1, Tnc, Fn1, and Ctss were upregulated.

claim: The upregulation of extracellular matrix components provided evidence for the compensatory hyperplasia of the extracellular matrix resulted in the pathologic fibrosis.
source: These provided evidence for the compensatory hyperplasia of the extracellular matrix resulted in the pathologic fibrosis, as well as the effective treatment strategies of targeted regulation of specific components of extracellular matrix (Ahmad, 2021).
evidence: Inferred from the upregulation of ECM components and their association with fibrosis, supported by citation to Ahmad, 2021

claim: Cortical malformations, including polymicrogyria, lissencephaly-pachygyria, and cobblestone, most severe in the occipital lobe, have been thought to be an important manifestation of the brain pathology in LAMA2-MD.
source: Recently, cortical malformations, including polymicrogyria, lissencephaly-pachygyria, and cobblestone, most severe in the occipital lobe, such as occipital pachygyria, have been thought to be an important manifestation of the brain pathology in LAMA2-MD (Jayakody et al., 2020; Camelo et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jayakody et al., 2020; Camelo et al., 2023

claim: During brain development, laminins are enriched at ventricular and pial surfaces and the BBB to mediate radial glial cells (RGCs) attachment for neuronal migration.
source: During brain development, laminins are enriched at ventricular and pial surfaces and the BBB to mediate radial glial cells (RGCs) attachment for neuronal migration.
evidence: Supported by established knowledge of brain development

claim: The abnormal neuronal migration in specific areas of the cortex due to the lack of RGCs attachment to the gliovascular basal lamina and consequent gaps in that membrane was associated with the cortical malformations.
source: The abnormal neuronal migration in specific areas of the cortex due to the lack of RGCs attachment to the gliovascular basal lamina and consequent gaps in that membrane, which was associated with the cortical malformations (Severino et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Severino et al., 2020

claim: Laminin α2 deficiency could result in an impaired gliovascular basal lamina of BBB, including altered integrity and composition of the endothelial basal lamina, abnormal pericytes and astrocytic endfeet.
source: In previous studies, it was reported that laminin α2 deficiency could result in an impaired gliovascular basal lamina of BBB, including altered integrity and composition of the endothelial basal lamina, abnormal pericytes and astrocytic endfeet (Devisme et al., 2012; Menezes et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Devisme et al., 2012; Menezes et al., 2014

claim: The aberrant BBB function was associated with the adhesion defect of alpha7 integrin subunit in astrocytes to laminins in the Itga7-/- mice.
source: As reported, the aberrant BBB function was also associated with the adhesion defect of alpha7 integrin subunit in astrocytes to laminins in the Itga7-/- mice (Chen et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2023

claim: Loss of communications involving the laminins' pathway between laminin α2 and integrins were predicted between vascular and leptomeningeal fibroblasts and astrocytes in the dyH/dyH brain.
source: In this study, loss of communications involving the laminins' pathway between laminin α2 and integrins were predicted between vascular and leptomeningeal fibroblasts and astrocytes in the dyH/dyH brain, providing more evidence for the impaired BBB due to laminin α2 deficiency.
evidence: Supported by cell-cell communication analysis from the study

claim: The cortical malformations were not found in the dyH/dyH brains by MRI analysis, probably due to the small volume within 1 month old.
source: Though the cortical malformations were not found in the dyH/dyH brains by MRI analysis, probably due to the small volume within 1 month old, the changes in transcriptomes and protein levels provided potentially useful data for the hypothesis of the impaired gliovascular basal lamina of the BBB, which might be associated with occipital pachygyria in LAMA2-CMD patients (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by MRI observations and inference about age-related limitations

claim: Seizures have been thought as a main symptom of brain dysfunctions in LAMA2-MD, which might be associated with cortical malformation.
source: Seizures have been thought as a main symptom of brain dysfunctions in LAMA2-MD, which might be associated with cortical malformation (Sarkozy et al., 2020; Huang et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Sarkozy et al., 2020; Huang et al., 2023

claim: The occurrence of seizures was thought to be related to the aberrant neuronal network formation and the imbalance of excitability and inhibitory neuronal network and ionic homeostasis.
source: The occurrence of seizures was thought to be related to the aberrant neuronal network formation and the imbalance of excitability and inhibitory neuronal network and ionic homeostasis (Barkovich et al., 2015; Jayakody et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Barkovich et al., 2015; Jayakody et al., 2020

claim: The dyH/dyH mouse model serves as a valid disease model for further investigation into the underlying pathogenesis of human LAMA2-CMD and developing effective therapeutic strategies.
